reason: E2 directly shows dynamic precipitation of M23C6 and σ phase in CoCrFeNiMn HEA under high-stress creep at 500–600 °C, and links it to increased stress exponent and activation energy, supporting the first three premises. However, E2 attributes the anomalous creep behavior to combined effects of recrystallization and precipitation, and E1 details how recrystallization alone increases the stress exponent, so the cited evidence does not support isolating precipitation's effect as proposed.
premises: Dynamic precipitation of M23C6 and Cr-rich σ phase occurs in high-entropy alloys under high-stress creep at 500–600 °C
Dynamic precipitation increases the stress exponent and activation energy for creep
Dynamic precipitation creates obstacles to dislocation motion, reducing creep rate
The effect of dynamic precipitation can be isolated from dynamic recrystallization
